note.p: . He was first a sword cutler, son of the highly esteemed sword cutler Thomas Gill of Birmingham. Later he became a patent agent, lived at 125 The Strand, and was for about 20 years, Chairman of Mechanics at the Royal Society of Arts, Manufacture and Commerce, in John Adam St. He produced upward of a dozen publications, Technical Resources, available on Google books. He was born 1773 in Birmingham, and died in Newington April 1856. He married Mary Sheffield in 1809, daughter of W E Sheffield. How many of the Gill's he accounts for is unclear. There is a period in 1814 of intense association with a 'Gill' - but it is unclear that this is the same Gill. And 'Mrs Gill' in 1807 is prior to Gill's marriage. Ed Pope is sceptical that this matches any entries - and none are currently coded.
